HERMES GSuite CLI Documentation

Welcome to the official documentation for HERMES GSuite CLI — a unified, AI-powered command-line interface designed to bring Google Workspace operations into a terminal-first workflow.

Architecture Principles

HERMES GSuite CLI is built on a centrally distributed, locally authenticated, client-side open-source architecture:

  • Client-Side Execution: HERMES runs entirely on your local machine. It connects directly to official Google Workspace APIs and the Google Gemini API. There are no intermediary proxy servers, third-party databases, or SaaS middlemen.
  • Individual OAuth 2.0 Authorization: Each user authorizes their own Google account independently. HERMES never shares a central developer account or collects user passwords.
  • Local User Isolation: Tokens (~/.config/gsuite-cli/token.json) and cache data (~/.cache/gsuite-cli/) are stored locally under your operating system user account.
  • Deterministic Execution: Direct commands execute directly with Google APIs. AI processing is isolated exclusively to explicit AI commands.

Quick Start

Get up and running with HERMES in less than two minutes:

bash
# 1. Install HERMES CLI from PyPI
pip install hermes-cli

# 2. Authenticate with your Google Account
hermes auth login

# 3. Check your calendar schedule
hermes calendar today

# 4. Triage your unread emails
hermes gmail list --max-results 5

Global CLI Options

The following global flags can be applied to any HERMES command:

Flag Description
--config-dir <path> Specify a custom directory for configuration and token storage instead of the default ~/.config/gsuite-cli/.
--format [table|json|csv] Set output formatting (default: table). Ideal for shell pipelines with jq.
--debug Enable verbose debugging logs to inspect HTTP requests and API responses.
--version Display the currently installed HERMES CLI version.
--help Print built-in command documentation and available options.
